facts.fact: The World Bank ICR says the private partners Portugal Telecom and CST (Companhia Sao Tomense de Telecomunicacoes) were to finance US$11.9 million of the ACE submarine cable participation through the STP-Cabo SARL special purpose vehicle, beside the US$13.1 million IDA grant; the ACE consortium is Orange-led and Portugal Telecom is Portuguese.

The ICR describes the ACE cable participation as a public-private partnership structured through the STP-Cabo SPV, in which the private partners Portugal Telecom and CST put in US$11.9 million alongside the government's IDA-financed share, with the grant effective in July 2011.

The ICR says CST, the Sao Tomean telecoms operator, secured about US$5 million of its share of the US$18.75 million STP-Cabo funding from debt and its own funds or cash flow; the document does not name the lender.

systems.owner: Government of STP, CST and Portugal Telecom shareholders; UNITEL from 2013

systems.system: UNITEL purchase of the state's 24.5% STP-Cabo stake and second licence

note: UNITEL's 2013 US$8 million (US$6.36 million for shares, US$1.62 million licence) went to the government, so it is class other; Baharicom's US$5 million philanthropic offer was withdrawn.
